title: Two housing rezonings deferred pending Region water information
subtitle: Courtland Avenue East high-rise proposal, Wimbleton Crescent semi-detached rezoning and a Siebert Avenue demolition request
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee recommended approval of a demolition request at 26 Siebert Avenue, where a single detached dwelling with an additional unit would be replaced by a new single detached home {{vote:m1}}.

The committee also referred two planning applications to the January 12, 2026 Council meeting. One is a proposal for 977 homes in towers up to 30 storeys at 808-836 Courtland Avenue East {{vote:m2}}. The other is a rezoning at 7 Wimbleton Crescent to allow semi-detached homes, each with an additional unit, for four units in total {{vote:m3}}. Staff asked for the delay because late Region comments on water servicing capacity needed review, and more Region information was expected the next day.

For residents, no final decision on either project was made at this meeting. Both return to Council on January 12, where people who spoke or wrote in can register to speak again. Neighbours on Wimbleton Crescent raised concerns about size, drainage, parking and how the application was described. On Courtland, school bus pick-up and traffic access were the main open questions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving demolition of a single detached dwelling with an attached additional unit, to be replaced by a new single detached dwelling.

The committee referred the Official Plan and zoning amendments, and the urban design brief endorsement, for a 977-unit, up-to-30-storey mixed-use development to the January 12 Council meeting so staff can consider more Region information.
The committee referred the rezoning from Residential Two to Residential Four, to allow semi-detached dwellings, to the January 12 Council meeting pending additional Region information.

debate: On Courtland, a councillor raised concern about left turns into the site at peak times near the highway ramps. The applicant's representative said the City, Region and Ministry of Transportation were consulted and a revised traffic analysis was accepted. A formal access permit is still needed at site plan stage.

Councillors were frustrated that school bus pick-up and drop-off for the Courtland towers is unresolved, since the Catholic school board will not enter private property. Staff said school boards set stops once the building is occupied and enrolment is known, and one councillor asked that the ward councillor be told the outcome.

Staff asked for the Courtland deferral because updated Region comments on water servicing capacity arrived late. Councillors asked about displaced businesses and affordability; the applicant's representative said tenants are on short-term leases with no compensation required, and affordable unit numbers are not yet known.

Wimbleton Crescent neighbours opposed the rezoning, citing neighbourhood character, ageing sewers, stormwater runoff, loss of trees, shadowing, privacy, parking, tandem driveways and property upkeep. Staff said engineering staff had no servicing concerns and that grading would be reviewed later.

Councillors said notices should have been clearer that four units were involved, and one apologized for the confusion. Staff and councillors noted that four units are already allowed as of right, and some supported the intensification. One councillor planned to seek a height cap of about nine metres when the item returns.
